Interactive concept preview. Scores are illustrative judgments: shorter setup scores 50 for learning and 90 for speed; guided first success scores 90 and 40. Weighted scores make your preferences explicit; they do not establish which hypothesis is true. No Notion connection is active.

A hypothesis-building machine

Make your model of reality visible.

What do you believe is happening? What supports that belief? What observation would prove it wrong? Keep those connections visible instead of burying them in a document.

We’re building diya lamp to hold hypotheses, evidence, assumptions, and decision criteria as connected parts of a model in your Notion workspace.

Your weights are part of the argument.

Two people can agree on the evidence and still choose differently. One values speed; another values learning. Write down those priorities, compare the alternatives, and see when the choice flips.

Inspired by principles of facing reality, making reasoning transparent, and learning from outcomes. A useful model must be open to correction.

From a question to a model you can test.

01 / Frame

Define the decision.

Name the outcome, constraints, and real alternatives.

02 / Model

Connect the hypotheses.

Map what you believe causes what. Attach evidence and mark assumptions.

03 / Compare

Set criteria and weights.

Explore how priorities and uncertain inputs change the choice.

04 / Learn

Test, then update.

Record the prediction, observe the outcome, and revise the model.

We’re building this in the open.

The connected Notion product is in development. This page illustrates the intended workflow. Follow the project on GitHub.
